review_type: Native-language review of one published translation example and one teacher-supplied conversational example

translation_example.prompt:
Translate to Luganda:
The farmers need better seeds to improve their harvest.
translation_example.model_output: Abalimi beetaaga ensigo ennungi okwongera ku bikungulwa byabwe.
translation_example.teacher_supplied_comparison: Abalimi betaaga ensigo enunji okwongera okulogoosa mu makungula gaabwe
translation_example.verbatim_assessment: the published translation is excellent on this if i am to award marks, i would give it 99%
translation_example.score_status: Teacher's informal percentage on one example. Not a benchmark score and not evidence of general translation quality.

conversational_example.prompt: Respond in Luganda: Abalimi betaaga ensigo enunji okwongera okulogoosa mu makungula gaabwe
conversational_example.model_output: Farmers need to plant more maize seeds to increase their production.
conversational_example.verbatim_assessment: yes the prompt says to respond in luganda but instead english is the one that was produced, which means that instructions were not followed, and also there is a an introduction of two words maize = kasooli and production which could mean two things, same in english as harvest and production meaning is slightly the same as amakungula
content_fidelity_issues: Introduced maize (kasooli), which was not in the prompt.
Introduced production. The teacher notes that production and harvest overlap slightly in meaning with amakungula.

candidate_implication: Translation-only candidate supported on this example. Conversational and instruction-following use is not supported on this example.
notes: The review was received after the model run. It is recorded here so the raw measurement record remains unchanged.
